title: Construction of a New Co(II) Coordination Polymer
one_line_summary: Design rule: use a mixed-ligand self-assembly strategy combining isophthalic acid and 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: hydrogen-bonded framework involving coordinated water, free water, carboxylate oxygen atoms, and amino groups of ATAZ → stability

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use a mixed-ligand self-assembly strategy combining isophthalic acid and 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole → effective construction of coordination polymers and successful formation of the target 3D pillar-layer framework

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] select organic ligands and metal ions with suitable coordination geometries → improves the likelihood of preparing target coordination compounds

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: methylene blue degradation system with compound 1 as catalyst vs methylene blue degradation system without compound 1 as catalyst: winner=subject_a on methylene_blue_degradation

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] operate or heat the framework above 350 C: the framework begins to collapse beyond 350 C

notable_quotes: A new Co(II) coordination polymer, [Co2(mbdc)(ATAZ)2(H2O)2]n·nH2O, was synthesized solvothermally/hydrothermally from Co(NO3)2, isophthalic acid and 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole.
Compound 1 forms a 3D pillar-layer framework built from Co(II)-ATAZ layers pillared by mbdc2−, and simplifies to a noninterpenetrated 6-connected pcu network.
Compound 1 is phase-pure by PXRD and shows stepwise water loss: 3.82% at 71–100 °C for free water and 7.18% at 150–200 °C for coordinated water.
